question: Calcium sulphate hemihydrates is the chemical name for:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plaster of Paris.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• ​CaSO4⋅12H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-8-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">​CaSO4⋅12H2O​CaSO4⋅12H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-43-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">​CaSO4⋅12H2O​CaSO4⋅12H2O ​CaSO4⋅12H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \text{H}_2\text{O} ​CaSO4⋅12H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \text{H}_2\text{O} ​CaSO4⋅12H2O\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \text{H}_2\text{O} CaSO4​⋅21​H2​O.
 
 
 
• It is commonly known as **plaster of Paris** and is formed by the partial hydration of gypsum
 
 
• (which is calcium sulfate dihydrate, CaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-9-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">CaSO4⋅2H2OCaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-44-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">CaSO4⋅2H2OCaSO4⋅2H2O CaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O} CaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O} CaSO4⋅2H2O\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O} CaSO4​⋅2H2​O).
 
 
 
• **When the plaster of Paris is mixed with water, it rehydrates and hardens, making it suitable for construction, art, and medical applications **
 
 
• **​**(like casts for broken bones).

• **Washing soda**: This is sodium carbonate (Na2CO3⋅10H2O \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-10-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Na2CO3⋅10H2ONa2CO3⋅10H2O \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-45-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Na2CO3⋅10H2ONa2CO3⋅10H2O Na2CO3⋅10H2O \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O} Na2CO3⋅10H2O \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O} Na2CO3⋅10H2O\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O} Na2​CO3​⋅10H2​O), used in cleaning and laundry.
 
• **Gypsum**: This is calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-11-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">CaSO4⋅2H2OCaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}" id="MathJax-Element-46-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">CaSO4⋅2H2OCaSO4⋅2H2O CaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O} CaSO4⋅2H2O \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O} CaSO4⋅2H2O\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O} CaSO4​⋅2H2​O), which is not the same as plaster of Paris.
 
• **Baking powder**: This is a leavening agent typically containing sodium bicarbonate and acid, used in baking.
